holidays.name: National Corn on the Cob Day
holidays.description: Fire up the grill or boil a big pot of water, because today is for butter-slathered, napkin-demanding corn eaten straight off the cob. Bonus points for the satisfying typewriter-style nibble from one end to the other.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance that arrives just as fresh sweet corn starts showing up at summer markets and cookouts. Its creator is unclear, but it has become a fixture on fun-holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: An ear of corn almost always has an even number of kernel rows, usually 14 to 18, and each ear grows roughly 800 kernels.

holidays.name: National German Chocolate Cake Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the tender chocolate layer cake with gooey coconut-pecan frosting. Despite the name, there's nothing German about the dessert's origins, and it's every bit as American as apple pie.
holidays.origin: The cake is named for Sam German, an English-American baker who developed a mild dark baking chocolate for the Baker's Chocolate Company in 1852. A Dallas newspaper printed a recipe for 'German's Chocolate Cake' in 1957. It spread fast, and the possessive eventually dropped away, so people assumed the cake came from Germany.
holidays.funFact: The cake's name comes from a person's surname, not a country. After the recipe was published, sales of Baker's German's Sweet Chocolate jumped dramatically.

holidays.name: King Kamehameha Day
holidays.description: Hawaii honors Kamehameha the Great with parades, floral processions, hula, and lei draping. Riders on horseback dressed in the colors of the islands take part. The statue of the king in Honolulu is covered in enormous flower leis.
holidays.origin: Kamehameha I united the Hawaiian Islands into one kingdom in 1810. King Kamehameha V established the holiday in 1871 to honor his grandfather's legacy, and Hawaii has marked it ever since.
holidays.funFact: The famous Kamehameha statue in Honolulu is a replica. The original was lost at sea off the Falkland Islands on its way to Hawaii, and it was later recovered and now stands in Kapaau on the Big Island.
